name: Bagalkote
headline: Child marriage and a 2022 hijab-related exam boycott are the documented exits for girls.
summary: Bagalkote reporting links girls' school exit to child marriage, with the state offering gram panchayats a Rs 50,000 reward for preventing it, and records a student skipping SSLC in 2022 rather than remove a hijab. Farm-labour pressure on teenagers is asserted but thinly sourced.

reasons.detail: A child development project officer's mentoring reaches over 600 early-married girls in Bagalkot villages, a measure of how common early marriage is.
A Bagalkot student refused to remove her hijab and skipped an SSLC paper during the 2022 dress-code row.
During COVID livelihood loss, families married off girls under 18 as a cost-cutting step; officials received 186 complaints in July 2020 to June 2021 versus about 50 in 2019.
The Zilla Parishad created MGNREGA work for migrant youth and skilling in tailoring, dairy and computers, indicating job loss was driving family decisions about girls.
NGO programme in Bagalkot and Bijapur villages ran Class 9-10 tuition to counter girls' vulnerability to dropping out after poor performance; counts are for both districts combined.
Samata found 153 discontinued and 125 dropped-out girls across Bagalkot and Bijapur villages by March 2016, yet only 21 and 14 respectively were brought back.

responses.text: The state pays Rs 50,000 to gram panchayats that prevent child marriages and runs Children's Gram Sabhas.
Zilla Parishad used the 1098 helpline, the Surakshini tracking portal, weekly home visits and Child Welfare Committee counselling to stop child marriages (2020-21).
Samata ran Class 9-10 tuition and a dropout tracking tool in schools across Bagalkot and Bijapur villages, bringing back 14 dropped-out girls by March 2016.
